home.meta_title: NASA Explorer — missions, launches and discoveries in real time
home.meta_description: An independent space portal built on real NASA data: upcoming launches, missions operating right now, live ISS tracking, the Astronomy Picture of the Day and the historical mission archive.
home.hero_title_line1: Everything NASA is doing right now,
home.hero_title_line2: with the source next to the number.
home.hero_lede: Upcoming launches with a real countdown, the missions still operating today, where the ISS is, and the full archive of space exploration. Nothing invented: every figure links to the public API it came from.
home.hero_photo_alt: The “Cosmic Cliffs” of the Carina Nebula (NGC 3324) imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
home.hero_photo_credit: NGC 3324 · “Cosmic Cliffs” — NASA / ESA / CSA / STScI · JWST NIRCam
home.board_empty: No launches in the queried window.
home.apod_lede: Every day NASA publishes an image of the cosmos with an explanation written by a professional astronomer. Today's is served here, straight from the API.
home.apod_error: Today's picture could not be loaded
home.index_title: Eight ways through the space programme
home.index_missions_text: From Mercury to Artemis: dates, crew, figures and NASA archive media for each mission.
home.index_launches_text: Worldwide calendar with countdown, rocket, pad, target orbit and webcast.
home.index_active_text: Artemis, JWST, Perseverance and the ISS: objectives, timeline, instruments and trajectory.
home.index_solar_text: Orbital simulator of the eight planets and the probes still operating out there.
home.index_iss_text: Position, speed and ground track of the International Space Station on the map.
home.index_live_text: NASA TV and NASA en Español, with the current live stream resolved every half hour.
home.index_apod_text: The full Astronomy Picture of the Day archive, with a date picker and a random pick.
home.index_search_text: Search by mission, programme, decade or keyword across everything in the portal.
home.sources_nasa: picture of the day and Mars rover photos, fetched from the browser.
home.sources_images: historical and mission photography; every image links back to its original record.
home.sources_ll2: worldwide launch calendar; refreshed on every visit and baked every 15 days.
home.sources_iss: real-time position of the International Space Station.
home.sources_note: This is an independent educational project. It is not affiliated with NASA or any space agency. NASA archive imagery is public domain unless another author is credited; the historical mission files are hand-written and checked against the sources cited in each one.
home.exo_lede: confirmed planets beyond the Solar System. {esteAnio} of them were confirmed so far in {anio}, and the number climbs on its own: nobody types it in here.
home.index_exoplanets_text: How many worlds have been confirmed beyond the Solar System, how they were found and this year's latest.

exoplanets.title: Exoplanets
exoplanets.subtitle: How many planets have been confirmed beyond the Solar System, how they were detected and which are the latest. Data from the NASA Exoplanet Archive.
exoplanets.lede: confirmed planets beyond the Solar System. {esteAnio} have been added so far in {anio}.
exoplanets.methods_note: Almost none have been seen directly: most are inferred from the wobble they cause in their star, or from the shadow they cast crossing in front of it.
exoplanets.per_year_note: The last fifteen years. {anio} is still open, so its bar will keep growing.
exoplanets.recent_note: Radius in Earth radii and orbital period in days. Blanks are values the archive does not have yet: for microlensing, for instance, the period can almost never be measured.
